To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the class of concordance measures that are correlations of transformed random vectors can be characterized by a simple functional form and the attainability of matrices with such concordance entries can be determined analytically.

(i) a whole class of concordance measures can be characterized in terms of correlations of transformed random vectors and (ii) this class of concordances includes Spearman’s and Blomqvists’ as special cases.

the compatibility and attainability of matrices of correlation-based measures of concordances can be studied in a unified manner by means of the correlation of random variables, that a subclass of attainability of block Spearman’s matrices is proposed, and that the Cholesky decomposition of block matrices of van de Waerden’s coefficients has a simple analytical form.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the theoretical foundations of measures of concordances and their applications in insurance and risk analysis.
the construction of random vectors whose concordance measures of interest are compatible with a given matrix of such measures.
a fundamental problem of whether and how a given square matrix with entries of concordance measures can be realized by a random vector, which has important practical implications.

, in general, matrices of concordance measures cannot be realized by random variables.
the measures of concordances considered here are not only compatible, but also attainable.

for any matrix of such concordances there exist random variables such that the matrix can be realized by the corresponding matrix of concordances, and that the random variables can be constructed in a systematic way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the class of concordance measures studied in this thesis is compatible and attainable for all dimensions, and that block matrices of such measures are also attainable.
we have provided a systematic study of compatibility and attainability of matrices of correlation-based measures of concordances.

we have characterized and studied the properties of the class of correlation-based concordance measures, which is a class of measures of concordances of random variables that are widely used in insurance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the class of concordance measures we consider can be used to construct compatible and attainable matrices of concordance for practical applications in risk management.
